title: South Sudan - Gold and Mineral Deposits
content:
South Sudan Geological and Mining Profile:

COUNTRY OVERVIEW:
- Area: 619,745 km²
- Capital: Juba
- Major geological units: Nile Congo Craton, Ubangian Belt, Mozambique Belt
- Primary mineralization: gold, diamonds, iron ore, manganese, chromite

KEY GOLD DEPOSITS:
1. Kidepo Area (Central Equatoria)
   - Alluvial gold in Kidepo River system
   - Grade: 0.5-2.0 g/m³ in gravels
   - Host: Precambrian metamorphic basement
   - Status: Active artisanal mining

2. Kapoeta Area (Eastern Equatoria)
   - Placer gold in seasonal rivers
   - Grade: 0.3-1.5 g/m³
   - Associated minerals: garnet, magnetite, ilmenite
   - Infrastructure: road access from Juba (dry season only)

3. Boma Area (Jonglei State)
   - Alluvial gold in Boma River tributaries
   - Grade: 0.2-1.0 g/m³
   - Large-scale potential: under-explored

4. Wau Area (Western Bahr el Ghazal)
   - Gold-quartz veins in Precambrian schist
   - Hard rock potential: grades unknown, early exploration
   - Associated: copper, lead, zinc occurrences

5. Maridi Area (Western Equatoria)
   - Alluvial gold in Maridi River
   - Grade: 0.4-1.8 g/m³
   - Artisanal mining active, ~5,000 miners estimated

DIAMOND DEPOSITS:
- Kafia Enclaves: alluvial diamonds reported, small scale
- Boma-Jonglei border: kimberlite indicator minerals found
- Status: Exploration stage

MINING REGULATIONS:
- Mining Act 2009 (transitional provisions)
- Ministry of Mining oversees licensing
- Artisanal mining permits available for citizens
- Large-scale exploration licenses: 4-year initial, renewable
- Environmental Impact Assessment required

INFRASTRUCTURE CHALLENGES:
- Limited road network (150km paved roads total)
- No rail network
- Seasonal flooding restricts access (May-November)
- Limited power grid (mainly diesel generators)
- Banking system developing — gold often traded in cash

title: Kenya - Gold, Gemstones, and Mineral Deposits
content:
Kenya Geological and Mining Profile:

COUNTRY OVERVIEW:
- Area: 580,367 km²
- Capital: Nairobi
- Major geological units: Tanzania Craton, Mozambique Belt, Kenya Rift
- Primary mineralization: gold, gemstones (tsavorite, rhodolite), titanium, soda ash

KEY GOLD DEPOSITS:
1. Kakamega Goldfield (Western Kenya)
   - Greenstone belt gold deposits
   - Grades: 2-15 g/t (hard rock), 0.5-3.0 g/m³ (alluvial)
   - Host rocks: Archean metavolcanics and metasediments
   - Active mines: Artisanal and small-scale
   - Potential: >100 tonnes Au endowment (under-explored)

2. Migori Gold Belt (Nyanza Province)
   - Shear-zone hosted gold-quartz veins
   - Grades: 3-12 g/t
   - Strike length: >30km
   - Infrastructure: 400km from Mombasa port

3. Siakago Area (Eastern Province)
   - Alluvial gold in Tana River tributaries
   - Grades: 0.3-2.0 g/m³
   - Artisanal mining: ~3,000 miners

4. Lolgorien Area (Narok County)
   - Gold in Archean greenstone belt
   - Grades: 2-8 g/t (hard rock)
   - Associated: silver, copper

GEMSTONE DEPOSITS:
1. Tsavorite (Green Garnet)
   - Location: Voi, Taita-Taveta County
   - Grades: 0.5-5.0 g/t in schist host rock
   - World's largest tsavorite deposit
   - Value: $500-$5,000/ct

2. Rhodolite Garnet
   - Location: Merelani Hills (adjacent to Tanzanian deposits)
   - Grades: 2-10 g/t in mica schist
   - Value: $200-$3,000/ct

3. Sapphire and Ruby
   - Location: Taita-Taveta, Makueni
   - Secondary deposits in volcanic laterite
   - Grades: variable, small-scale mining

MINING REGULATIONS:
- Mining Act 2016
- Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority
- Environmental Impact Assessment mandatory
- Community Development Agreements required
- Artisanal mining license: KES 5,000 fee

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- Paved road network: 18,000km
- Standard gauge railway: Mombasa-Nairobi
- Major port: Mombasa (container and bulk)
- Power grid: 80% national coverage
- Mobile money (M-Pesa) facilitates gold trade

title: Uganda - Gold, Cobalt, and Mineral Deposits
content:
Uganda Geological and Mining Profile:

COUNTRY OVERVIEW:
- Area: 241,038 km²
- Capital: Kampala
- Major geological units: Tanzania Craton, Buganda-Toro Belt, Kibaran Belt
- Primary mineralization: gold, cobalt, copper, iron ore, tungsten, tin

KEY GOLD DEPOSITS:
1. Karamoja Gold Province (Northeastern Uganda)
   - Greenstone belt gold deposits
   - Grades: 2-20 g/t (hard rock)
   - Active mines: Artisanal mining in Moroto, Napak, Nakapiripirit districts
   - Potential: 50-200 tonnes Au endowment

2. Buhweju Gold Belt (Western Uganda)
   - Shear zone hosted gold-quartz veins
   - Grades: 5-25 g/t (high grade)
   - Strike length: >40km
   - Active ASGM operations: ~10,000 miners
   - Infrastructure: 300km from Mombasa via Kenya

3. Bulyanhulu Area (Tanzania border)
   - Extension of Tanzanian greenstone belt
   - Grades: 3-15 g/t
   - Potential for large-scale operations

4. Busia Goldfield (Eastern Uganda)
   - Alluvial gold in Lake Victoria basin
   - Grades: 0.5-3.0 g/m³
   - Cross-border with Kenyan deposits

COBALT DEPOSITS:
- Kasese (Albertine Rift): cobalt-copper deposits
- Grades: 0.1-0.5% Co in sediment-hosted copper
- Kilembe Mines: historical copper-cobalt producer
- Potential: 5,000-15,000 tonnes cobalt metal

OTHER MINERALS:
- Tin: Kitaka and Bufumbira volcanic fields
- Tungsten: Kigezi region, wolframite in quartz veins
- Iron ore: Muko deposits, 160 million tonnes @ 45% Fe
- Marble: Tororo and Bugiri, commercial production

MINING REGULATIONS:
- Mining and Minerals Act 2003
- Energy and Mineral Resources sector
- Artisanal mining: license from District Mining Officer
- Large-scale: Environmental Impact Assessment + Mining License
- Export: gold must be assayed at government-certified lab

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- Paved roads: 7,000km
- Railway: Meter gauge (Uganda Railways)
- Port access: Mombasa (800km from Kampala)
- Power: 60% national coverage, hydro + thermal
- Gold trade: Kampala is regional gold trading hub

title: Democratic Republic of Congo - Gold, Diamonds, and Strategic Minerals
content:
DRC Geological and Mining Profile:

COUNTRY OVERVIEW:
- Area: 2,344,858 km²
- Capital: Kinshasa
- Major geological units: Congo Craton, Kibaran Belt, Lufilian Arc, Ituri Arc
- Primary mineralization: gold, diamonds, coltan, cobalt, copper, tin, tungsten
- One of the most mineral-rich countries on Earth

KEY GOLD DEPOSITS:
1. Ituri Province (northeastern DRC)
   - Kibali Gold Mine: largest in DRC, 600,000 oz/year production
   - Grades: 2-5 g/t (open pit), 8-20 g/t (underground)
   - Host: Archean greenstone belt
   - Operator: Barrick Gold Corporation

2. Mambasa Area (Ituri Province)
   - Artisanal gold mining: estimated 20,000+ miners
   - Alluvial and hard rock deposits
   - Grades: 1-10 g/t
   - Infrastructure challenges: limited road access

3. South Kivu (Eastern DRC)
   - Gold in schist-hosted shear zones
   - Grades: 3-15 g/t
   - Active artisanal mining
   - Conflict mineral concerns

4. Kasaï Provinces (Central DRC)
   - Alluvial gold in Kasaï River system
   - Grades: 0.5-3.0 g/m³
   - Large-scale potential under-explored

5. Maniema Province
   - Gold-quartz veins in metamorphic basement
   - Grades: 2-8 g/t
   - Artisanal mining dominant

DIAMOND DEPOSITS:
- Kasai Province: world's largest alluvial diamond field
- Historical production: >10 million carats/year (peak)
- Grades: 0.5-2.0 carats/m³ gravel
- Quality: industrial to gem grade
- Major mines: MIBA, Société Minière de Bakwanga

STRATEGIC MINERALS:
1. Coltan (Columbite-Tantalite)
   - North Kivu and Maniema: 80% of world's coltan reserves
   - Critical for electronics (capacitors, smartphones)
   - Artisanal mining: 30,000+ miners
   - Price: $50-$300/kg depending on Ta₂O₅ grade

2. Cobalt
   - Katanga Province: 70% of world's cobalt production
   - Copper-cobalt belt: sediment-hosted deposits
   - Grades: 0.1-0.5% Co
   - Major mines: Tenke Fungurume, Katanga Mining

3. Tin (Cassiterite)
   - North Kivu and Maniema
   - Conflict mineral: used in electronics
   - Artisanal mining dominant

4. Tungsten (Wolframite)
   - Walikale and Masisi territories
   - Grades: 0.5-2.0% WO₃

MINING REGULATIONS:
- Mining Code 2002 (revised 2018)
- 10% royalty on strategic minerals
- Artisanal mining: authorized in designated zones
- Export certificate: CEIC (Certificate of Origin)
- Due diligence: OECD guidelines for conflict minerals

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- Road network: 152,000km (only 2.7% paved)
- Rail: 3,641km (colonial era, limited operation)
- River transport: Congo River system (vital for interior)
- Power: 19% national coverage (lowest in Africa)
- Major ports: Matadi (Atlantic), Mombasa (for eastern DRC via Uganda)

ARTISANAL MINING SCALE:
- Estimated 2 million artisanal miners (creuseurs)
- 10% of population depends on artisanal mining
- Gold production: 20-30 tonnes/year (official), estimated 40-50 tonnes total
- Diamond production: 15-20 million carats/year

title: Tanzania - Gold, Gemstones, and Mineral Deposits
content:
Tanzania Geological and Mining Profile:

COUNTRY OVERVIEW:
- Area: 945,087 km²
- Capital: Dodoma
- Major geological units: Tanzania Craton, Mozambique Belt, Karoo Supergroup
- Primary mineralization: gold, diamonds, tanzanite, rubies, iron ore, coal
- Africa's 4th largest gold producer

KEY GOLD DEPOSITS:
1. Geita Gold Mine (Lake Victoria Goldfield)
   - Largest mine in Tanzania: 500,000+ oz/year
   - Grades: 2-4 g/t (open pit)
   - Host: Archean greenstone belt
   - Operator: AngloGold Ashanti

2. North Mara Gold Mine (Tarime)
   - Production: 300,000+ oz/year
   - Grades: 1.5-3.0 g/t
   - Underground and open pit
   - Operator: Barrick Gold

3. Bulyanhulu Mine (Shinyanga)
   - Underground mine: one of the deepest in Africa (1,500m)
   - Grades: 8-15 g/t (high grade)
   - Gold-silver-copper mineralization
   - Operator: Barrick Gold

4. Geita Greenstone Belt
   - Multiple deposits along 100km strike
   - Total endowment: >30 million ounces
   - Active large-scale and artisanal mining

5. Musoma-Kahama Belt
   - Alluvial and hard rock gold
   - Grades: 2-10 g/t (hard rock)
   - Artisanal mining: 50,000+ miners

6. Lupa Goldfield (Mbeya)
   - Historical producer
   - Grades: 3-15 g/t
   - Under-explored, potential for new discoveries

GEMSTONE DEPOSITS:
1. Tanzanite (Blue Zoisite)
   - Location: Merelani Hills, Arusha (only known source)
   - Discovery: 1967
   - Grades: 1-5 carats per tonne
   - Value: $200-$50,000/ct depending on quality
   - Production: 2,000-3,000 kg/year
   - Depth: 60-400m below surface

2. Ruby (Winza Ruby)
   - Location: Dodoma Region
   - Quality: comparable to Burmese ruby
   - Discovered: 2007
   - Production: small-scale

3. Tsavorite
   - Location: Simanjiro District
   - Grades: 0.5-3.0 g/t
   - Value: $500-$5,000/ct

DIAMOND DEPOSITS:
- Mwadui (Williamson Diamond Mine): one of the oldest diamond mines
   - Production: 500,000+ carats/year
   - Open pit: 1.2km diameter, 400m deep
   - kimberlite pipe
- Alluvial diamonds in Rufiji River system

MINING REGULATIONS:
- Mining Act 2010 (amended 2017)
- Mining Commission: regulatory body
- Artisanal mining license: TZS 500,000
- Large-scale: Environmental Impact Assessment + Mining License
- Local content requirements: 5% of procurement to local suppliers
- Mineral royalty: 3-7% depending on mineral

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- Road network: 114,000km (4,000km paved)
- Railway: TAZARA (Dar es Salaam-Zambia), Central Line
- Ports: Dar es Salaam (main), Tanga, Mtwara
- Power: 45% national coverage, hydro + natural gas
- Air: multiple domestic airports for mining regions

PRODUCTION:
- Gold: 50+ tonnes/year (Africa's 4th largest producer)
- Diamonds: 2+ million carats/year
- Tanzanite: 2,000+ kg/year
- Total mining contribution: 6-8% of GDP
